text.title: Stocks surge as Nvidia jumps 31% on Huang's return; S&P 500 +4.7%, Nasdaq +6.5%
text.summary: US equities staged their biggest rebound in over a year after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, reviving the AI trade that drove last week's selloff. The S&P 500 gained 4.7% to 7237.17, the Nasdaq rose 6.5% and the Dow added 3.0%, while the VIX eased 6.4% to 26.62. Treasury yields were roughly flat to slightly higher as money moved into riskier assets, and the dollar firmed 0.5% to a one-month high. Oil fell 3.6% while gold bounced 3.3%. The common thread was a relief rally in the stocks that led the market lower, even though most indexes remain well below their recent highs.
text.rates: The 10-year Treasury yield edged up 1 bp to 4.92% and the 2-year was unchanged at 4.63%. WSJ tied the modest rise in US yields to investors moving into riskier assets. Both yields are still about 20 bp lower than five days ago. New York Fed President Williams said higher interest rates are likely over time to address inflation, though he expects inflation to move closer to 2% in 2027, and that kept rate expectations in focus. The dollar index gained 0.5% to 104.33, a one-month high, while falling oil eased the inflation backdrop. Equities largely ignored the rate moves in favor of the AI rebound.
text.breadth: Participation was broad. Every sector except staples and energy gained, and the Russell 2000 rose 3.4% against 4.7% for the S&P 500, so small caps joined in but trailed. Technology's 9.0% jump and the Nasdaq's outperformance show growth leading value, and cyclicals beat defensives. The VIX fell 6.4% to 26.62 but remains 16.2% above where it stood five days ago, so investors have not yet fully relaxed.
text.context: Today's rally snapped a seven-session S&P 500 losing streak. The S&P 500 is still 2.4% lower over five days and 6.5% below its one-month high, and the Nasdaq is 9.3% below its high. J.P. Morgan's weekly recap shows the S&P 500 fell 8.6% last week and the Nasdaq 10.0%, with growth stocks hit hardest. It put the S&P 500 at 16.4x forward earnings as of Nov 20.
text.takeaway: A single-day gain of this size, following a selloff of similar scale, shows how sharply markets can swing when sentiment around a concentrated theme like AI changes. For long-term diversified investors, it is a reminder that daily moves can be large in both directions and that concentrated leadership drives index results.
text.talk: Stocks bounced sharply today after Nvidia brought back Jensen Huang as CEO, which restored confidence in the AI trade after last week's steep selloff. Indexes are still below their recent highs, so volatility remains elevated.

drivers.t: Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, and the stock jumped about 31%. Reuters reported the board reversed itself after Trump intervened, and CNBC said the board had input from senior US government levels. Huang had resigned on Nov. 12. Nvidia sits at the center of AI spending and index weights, so a swing of this size moved the whole market. The tech sector rose 9.0% and the Nasdaq had its best day since April 2025. MarketWatch described the rebound as relief for a battered AI trade.

Oracle, CoreWeave and other cloud names rallied as investors bet the AI cash will keep flowing. MarketWatch notes that Nvidia's financing of the ecosystem has been crucial to these companies. A more stable Nvidia lowers the perceived risk that the funding chain behind data-center buildouts breaks down. Short sellers were hit hard, as leveraged products betting against Nvidia were nearly wiped out. WSJ noted that credit markets were less enthusiastic about the reinstatement.

Consumer staples slipped 0.1% and energy fell 1.1%, the only two sectors in the red. MarketWatch said consumer stocks, seen as safe amid cracks in the AI trade, were among the S&P 500's biggest losers, with Kroger and Tyson Foods lower. When risk appetite returns, money tends to rotate out of defensive holdings toward growth. Cyclical groups led, with consumer discretionary up 4.0%, industrials up 3.9% and communication services up 3.6%.

Crude settled at its lowest since August as oil kept flowing out of the Persian Gulf despite continued attacks on shipping. Traders are also weighing an expected global supply surplus. WTI fell 3.6% to 80.37 and is down 22.2% over a month. Lower crude eases pressure on energy-sensitive inflation, but it weighed on the energy sector. Natural gas also had its biggest one-day drop since February on milder weather forecasts.
drivers.impact: Oil and gas lower, energy lags

drivers.t: Gold bounced 3.3% to 3632.5, ending a three-session slide that included its steepest weekly drop since March. WSJ said the metals rose as the Nvidia news lifted equities and other assets. The move suggests the bounce was a broad risk-on rebound rather than a flight to safety. Gold remains 5.7% lower over five days and 11.7% below its one-month high.

earnings.t: The stock fell 5.5% after hours even though HPE raised its forecast on strong AI demand and posted its strongest growth ever, per MarketWatch. That suggests expectations were already high.

watch.why: The forecast is 92.4 versus 91.7 previously, and it gives a read on household sentiment amid the market swings.
